project.name: AtlasWeave
project.summary: A visual thinking and learning board inside Obsidian. Ideas, frames, tables, code and equations save together as Mermaid.

nodes.label: Board workspace
nodes.summary: Lets people arrange ideas, edit text and work with tables, code and equations.

nodes.label: Editing ideas
nodes.summary: Turns pointer and keyboard gestures into board changes and formatted text.

nodes.label: Drawing connections
nodes.summary: Places shapes, routes connectors and keeps labels and attachment points readable.

nodes.label: Saved board rules
nodes.summary: Preserves Mermaid content, frame ownership, arrangement and text formatting.

nodes.label: Copying and pasting
nodes.summary: Imports editable content and exports selections as Mermaid or images.

nodes.label: Obsidian connection
nodes.summary: Opens board files, saves changes, resolves vault links and exposes preferences.

nodes.label: Agent connection
nodes.summary: Lets an external assistant read or change a board through the optional local bridge.

nodes.label: Verification
nodes.summary: Checks board behavior, document round trips, routing and browser interactions.

nodes.label: Development tools
nodes.summary: Builds and checks the plugin and prepares its local architecture map.

nodes.label: Obsidian vault
nodes.summary: Stores board files and the notes that ideas link to.

nodes.label: Mermaid diagrams
nodes.summary: Reads diagram source and supplies the initial arrangement of imported diagrams.

flows.title: Edit an idea and save it

steps.note: The board collects an edit and creates the next document.
The document becomes validated Mermaid source.
Obsidian writes the updated source back to the vault.
The clipboard content is recognized and decoded.
The board validates the incoming shapes and connections.
The board measures and displays the editable result.

flows.title: Change a board through an assistant

steps.note: The assistant calls a board tool.
The local bridge checks access and handles the request.
Validated operations produce the new board document.
